types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign nation-state recognized as a political entity. Also called nation, state, republic, nation-state. Examples: Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, France, DR Congo.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are sovereign nations; schema.org Country matches exactly.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: InternationalOrganization: An organization composed of multiple sovereign states that operates across national borders. Also called intergovernmental organization, global body, multinational agency, world body. Examples: World Health Organization, WHO.

chosen_type.label: MedicalOrganization
chosen_type.justification: World Health Organization is a health‑focused organization, fitting MedicalOrganization.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, figure, personage. Examples: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Dr Samuel Roger Kamba, Pregnant woman (Ebola positive), Suspected Ebola patient.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are individual humans; schema.org Person is appropriate.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

types.embedding_query_text: VirusSpecies: A distinct taxonomic group of viruses sharing common characteristics. Also called viral strain, virus type, virus variant, viral species. Examples: Bundibugyo virus.

chosen_type.label: Taxon
chosen_type.justification: Bundibugyo virus is a biological species; Taxon captures taxonomic entities.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: DDxElement
candidates.comment: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

types.embedding_query_text: Disease: A medical condition characterized by specific signs and symptoms. Also called illness, ailment, infection, malady. Examples: Ebola.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: Ebola is a disease; MedicalCondition covers diseases and disorders.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalIndication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.

candidates.label: MedicalSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchInstitute: An organization dedicated to scientific research and development. Also called research center, laboratory, institute, research facility. Examples: Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale, Institute of Tropical Medicine.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Institutes described are research bodies; ResearchOrganization matches.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: MedicalClinic
candidates.comment: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.

types.embedding_query_text: University: An institution of higher education and research granting academic degrees. Also called college, academic institution, higher education, scholarly institute. Examples: University of Oxford.

chosen_type.label: CollegeOrUniversity
chosen_type.justification: University of Oxford is a higher‑education institution; CollegeOrUniversity is the exact class.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: Thesis
candidates.comment: A scholarly document submitted by a candidate for an academic degree or professional qualification. Also called dissertation, academic paper, research thesis. Examples: a PhD dissertation, a master's thesis, an undergraduate honors thesis.

types.embedding_query_text: Province: A primary administrative subdivision of a country. Also called region, state, district, administrative area. Examples: South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, Tshopo.

chosen_type.label: State
chosen_type.justification: The listed provinces are primary administrative subdivisions; State includes provinces.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

types.embedding_query_text: City: An urban settlement with a large population and administrative significance. Also called metropolis, town, municipality, urban center. Examples: Kinshasa, Geneva, Kisangani.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Kinshasa, Geneva, Kisangani are urban settlements; City is the correct class.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

types.embedding_query_text: ArmedGroup: An organized group that uses armed force to achieve political or territorial objectives. Also called militia, rebel group, insurgent group, armed faction. Examples: M23 rebel group, M23.

chosen_type.label: ArmedGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organized group that uses armed force to pursue political or territorial objectives.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class captures rebel/armed groups; mint under Organization.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific calendar day or period expressed in a standardized format. Also called calendar date, day, time point, date stamp. Examples: 2 July 2026, 1 July 2026, May 2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are calendar dates; schema.org Date matches.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: CaseCount: A numeric value representing the number of reported cases, deaths, or recoveries of a disease. Also called tally, count, statistic, figure. Examples: 1,460 confirmed cases, 452 deaths, 213 recoveries, 150 suspected cases.

chosen_type.label: CaseCount
chosen_type.definition: A numeric count representing the number of reported disease cases, deaths, or recoveries.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class models case counts; mint as an Intangible quantitative value.

candidates.label: RsvpResponseType
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing the possible responses to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply type. Examples: RsvpResponseType.Yes, RsvpResponseType.No, RsvpResponseType.MayBe.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

chosen_type.label: Drug
chosen_type.justification: Reference to antiviral drugs fits the Drug product class.

candidates.label: DrugStrength
candidates.comment: A DrugStrength is a MedicalIntangible representing a specific potency in which a medical drug is available in a particular country. Also called medication dosage, pharmaceutical concentration. Examples: "500 mg tablets", "10 mg/mL solution", "25 mcg patch".

candidates.label: DrugPrescriptionStatus
candidates.comment: A DrugPrescriptionStatus is a MedicalEnumeration indicating whether a drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter. Also called medication availability, prescription requirement. Examples: PrescriptionOnly, OverTheCounter.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: DrugClass
candidates.comment: A DrugClass is a MedicalEntity representing a category of medical drugs, grouped by general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, or physiological effects. Also called drug category, medication group, therapeutic class. Examples: Statins, Antibiotics, Antidepressants, Beta-blockers.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

chosen_type.label: FacilityCount
chosen_type.definition: A numeric count indicating the number of facilities (e.g., laboratories) of a given type.
chosen_type.justification: No existing class for counts of facilities; mint under Intangible.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: MedicalTrialDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for medical trials. Also called clinical trial design, trial methodology, study architecture. Examples: "RandomizedControlledTrial", "SingleBlindTrial", "DoubleBlindTrial", "CrossoverTrial".

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".

candidates.label: CovidTestingFacility
candidates.comment: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The expression "2 to 21 days" denotes a time span; Duration captures this.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: DoseSchedule
candidates.comment: A DoseSchedule is a MedicalIntangible specifying a particular regimen for administering a drug or supplement. Also called dosing regimen, medication schedule, treatment plan. Examples: "Take one pill daily", "Apply twice a day for 7 days", "Administer 500mg every 8 hours".
